_comment: Stowage codes (16a), handling codes (16a) and segregation codes (16b) with their descriptions, taken from chapters 7.1.5, 7.1.6 and 7.2.8 of the IMDG Code. A compilation of facts offered as an aid; the published text of the code remains authoritative. Read by machine with scripts/extract_imdg_codes.py.
source: IMO-resolutie MSC.556(108), aangenomen 23 mei 2024 — Amendments to the International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code, Amendment 42-24, in werking sinds 1 januari 2026

codes.SW3: Shall be transported under temperature control.
codes.SW4: Surface ventilation is required to assist in removing any residual solvent vapour.
codes.SW5: If under deck, stow in a mechanically ventilated space.
codes.SW6: When stowed under deck, mechanical ventilation shall be in accordance with SOLAS regulation II-2/19 (II-2/54) for flammable liquids with flashpoint below 23°C c.c.
codes.SW7: As approved by the competent authorities of the countries involved in the shipment.
codes.SW8: Ventilation may be required. The possible need to open hatches in case of fire to provide maximum ventilation and to apply water in an emergency, and the consequent risk to the stability of the ship through flooding of the cargo spaces, shall be considered before loading.
codes.SW9: Provide a good through ventilation for bagged cargo. Double strip stowage is recommended. The illustration in 7.6.2.7.2.3 shows how this can be achieved. During the voyage regular temperature readings shall be taken at varying depths in the hold and recorded. If the temperature of the cargo exceeds the ambient temperature and continues to increase, ventilation shall be closed down.
codes.SW10: Unless carried in closed cargo transport units, bales shall be properly covered by tarpaulins or the like. Cargo spaces shall be clean, dry and free from oil or grease. Ventilator cowls leading into the cargo space shall have sparking-preventing screens. All other openings, entrances and hatches leading to the cargo space shall be securely closed. During temporary interruption of loading, when the hatch remains uncovered, a fire-watch shall be kept. During loading or discharge, smoking in the vicinity shall be prohibited and fire-fighting appliances kept ready for immediate operation.
codes.SW11: Cargo transport units shall be shaded from direct sunlight. Packages in cargo transport units shall be stowed so as to allow for adequate air circulation throughout the cargo.
codes.SW12: Taking account of any supplementary requirements specified in the transport documents.
codes.SW13: Taking account of any supplementary requirements specified in the competent authority approval certificate(s).
codes.SW14: Category A only if the special stowage provisions of 7.4.1.4 and 7.6.2.8.4 are complied with.
codes.SW15: For metal drums, stowage category B.
codes.SW16: For unit loads in open cargo transport units, stowage category B.
codes.SW17: Category E, for closed cargo transport unit and pallet boxes only. Ventilation may be required. The possible need to open hatches in case of fire to provide maximum ventilation and to apply water in an emergency, and the consequent risk to the stability of the ship through flooding of the cargo space, shall be considered before loading.
codes.SW18: Category A, when transported in accordance with P650.
codes.SW19: For batteries transported in accordance with special provisions 376 or 377, category C, unless transported on a short international voyage.
codes.SW20: For uranyl nitrate hexahydrate solution stowage, category D applies.
codes.SW21: For uranium metal pyrophoric and thorium metal pyrophoric stowage, category D applies.
codes.SW22: For AEROSOLS with a maximum capacity of 1 L: category A. For AEROSOLS with a capacity above 1 L: category B. For WASTE AEROSOLS or WASTE GAS CARTRIDGES: category C, clear of living quarters.
codes.SW23: When transported in BK3 bulk container, see 7.6.2.12 and 7.7.3.9.
codes.SW24: For special stowage provisions, see 7.4.1.3 and 7.6.2.7.2.
codes.SW26: For special stowage provisions, see 7.4.1.4 and 7.6.2.11.1.1.
codes.SW28: As approved by the competent authority of the country of origin.
codes.SW29: For engines or machinery containing fuels with flashpoint equal or greater than 23°C, stowage Category A.
codes.SW31: Stow away from potential sources of ignition, as determined in 7.4.2.3.2 or 7.5.2.8 or 7.6.2.2.2, as applicable.

codes.H1: Keep as dry as reasonably practicable.
codes.H2: Keep as cool as reasonably practicable.
codes.H3: During transport, it should be stowed (or kept) in a cool ventilated place.
codes.H4: If cleaning of cargo spaces has to be carried out at sea, the safety procedures followed and standard of equipment used shall be at least as effective as those employed as industry best practice in a port. Until such cleaning is undertaken, the cargo spaces in which the asbestos has been carried shall be closed and access to those spaces shall be prohibited.
codes.H5: Avoid handling the packaging or large packaging or keep handling to a minimum. Inform the appropriate public health authority or veterinary authority where persons or animals may have been exposed.

codes.SG1: For packages carrying a subsidiary hazard label of class 1, segregation as for class 1, division 1.3. However, in relation to goods of class 1, segregation as for the primary hazard.
codes.SG14: Stow “separated from” class 1 except for division 1.4S.
codes.SG23: Stow “away from” animal or vegetable oils.
codes.SG25: Stow “separated from” goods of classes 2.1 and 3.
codes.SG26: In addition: from goods of classes 2.1 and 3 when stowed on deck of a containership a minimum distance of two container spaces athwartship shall be maintained, when stowed on ro-ro ships a distance of 6 m athwartship shall be maintained.
codes.SG27: Stow “separated from” explosives containing chlorates or perchlorates.
codes.SG28: Stow “separated from” SGG2 – ammonium compounds and explosives containing ammonium compounds or salts.
codes.SG29: Segregation from foodstuffs as in 7.3.4.2.2, 7.6.3.1.2 or 7.7.3.7.
codes.SG30: Stow “away from” SGG7 – heavy metals and their salts.
codes.SG31: Stow “away from” SGG9 – lead and its compounds.
codes.SG32: Stow “away from” SGG10 – liquid halogenated hydrocarbons.
codes.SG34: When containing ammonium compounds, “separated from” SGG4 – chlorates or SGG13 – perchlorates and explosives containing chlorates or perchlorates.
codes.SG39: Stow “separated from” SGG2 – ammonium compounds other than AMMONIUM PERSULPHATE (UN 1444).
codes.SG40: Stow “separated from” SGG2 – ammonium compounds other than mixtures of ammonium persulphates and/or potassium persulphates and/or sodium persulphates.
codes.SG41: Stow “separated from” animal or vegetable oil.
codes.SG50: Segregation from foodstuffs as in 7.3.4.2.1, 7.6.3.1.2 or 7.7.3.6.
codes.SG53: Shall not be stowed together with combustible material in the same cargo transport unit.
codes.SG54: Stow “separated from” SGG11 – mercury and mercury compounds.
codes.SG63: Stow “separated longitudinally by an intervening complete compartment or hold from” class 1.
codes.SG65: Stow “separated by a complete compartment or hold from” class 1 except for division 1.4.
codes.SG67: Stow “separated from” division 1.4 and “separated longitudinally by an intervening complete compartment or hold from” divisions 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5 and 1.6 except from explosives of compatibility group J.
codes.SG68: If flashpoint 60°C c.c. or below, segregation as for class 3 but “away from” class 4.1.
codes.SG69: For AEROSOLS with a maximum capacity of 1 L: segregation as for class 9. Stow “separated from” class 1 except for division 1.4. For AEROSOLS with a capacity above 1 L: segregation as for the appropriate subdivision of class 2. For WASTE AEROSOLS: segregation as for the appropriate subdivision of class 2.
codes.SG70: For arsenic sulphides, “separated from” SGG1 – acids.
codes.SG71: Within the appliance, to the extent that the dangerous goods are integral parts of the complete life-saving appliance, there is no need to apply the provisions on segregation of substances in chapter 7.2.
codes.SG77: Segregation as for class 8. However, in relation to class 7, no segregation needs to be applied.
codes.SG78: Stow “separated longitudinally by an intervening complete compartment or hold from” division 1.1, 1.2, and 1.5.
